title: Image-sensor pinned photodiode recast as buried, interface-free DRAM storage well
idea: Borrow the CMOS image sensor's pinned photodiode: store the bit as electrons in a fully depleted buried n-well under a p+ pinning layer, read out through a transfer gate onto a floating diffusion exactly like a 4T pixel. The stored charge never touches a Si/SiO2 interface, so interface-trap SRH generation (the source of most of the <=13 fA tail) is shut off; a deep-trench vertical pinned well, as in stacked global-shutter pixels, supplies ~8-15k electrons.
why: Fact 3: CIS dark current is ~1-10 e-/s per pixel versus ~8x10^4 e-/s for a 13 fA DRAM tail cell; even a 100x leakage cut stretches refresh from 64 ms to seconds, cutting refresh energy and bandwidth loss 10-100x.

title: PERC solar trick: negative-charge alumina liners silence storage-junction surface leakage
idea: PERC solar cells keep minority carriers off the rear surface with ALD Al2O3 carrying ~10^13 cm^-2 negative fixed charge. Line the storage-node contact sidewall and STI edge, where the n+ junction meets a surface, with the same charged Al2O3 so holes accumulate in the p-well surface and the depletion region (and its interface-trap generation) is pushed off the surface.
why: Perimeter/surface generation is a large part of the junction-leakage tail (fact 3); field-effect passivation cut solar surface recombination ~10x, so 3-5x lower tail leakage and 2-4x longer refresh interval is plausible.

title: Solar-wafer gettering sinks buried under arrays to vacuum up tail metals
idea: Multicrystalline solar silicon became usable through phosphorus-diffusion and cavity gettering that pull Fe, Cu and Ni out of the active volume. Build a sacrificial gettering band 2-3 um under each DRAM array (carbon co-implant plus a hydrogen-implanted cavity layer, no scarce helium) and add a late low-temperature 'gettering soak' so transition-metal deep-level traps migrate away from storage junctions.
why: Retention-tail and VRT cells cluster at metal/defect sites; shrinking the tail 3-10x moves the refresh-limiting cell population and raises yield of 32-64 Gb dies (fact 3).

title: UNSW light-steered hydrogenation re-passivates deep access-transistor traps
idea: UNSW's 'advanced hydrogenation' for solar cells shines intense light during a 200-400 C anneal to set hydrogen's charge state (H0/H-), letting it diffuse far and bond to otherwise unreachable defects. Apply a flash-lamp or LED-illuminated hydrogenation step after capacitor formation so hydrogen reaches buried-wordline gate-oxide and channel traps hidden under the capacitor stack.
why: Interface traps under the buried gate drive GIDL and trap-assisted tunneling in the tail (fact 3); deeper, charge-state-controlled passivation could halve Dit and shrink tail leakage 2-5x.

title: TOPCon passivating contact replaces the implanted storage-node junction
idea: Solar TOPCon contacts reach saturation currents of ~5 fA/cm^2 by placing a 1.5 nm tunnel oxide between crystalline silicon and heavily doped poly-Si, so the defective metallurgical junction sits outside the crystal. Form the storage-node contact as a tunnel-oxide/n+ poly stack on an undoped channel tip: by reciprocity, a contact with near-zero recombination J0 also has near-zero generation (leakage) current.
why: Junction generation is a core part of the <=13 fA tail (fact 3); a contact that gave solar cells 10-100x lower J0 could cut junction leakage ~10x and extend refresh 4-10x.

title: Low-self-discharge battery separator: crested tunnel barrier in storage-node contact
idea: Low-self-discharge NiMH cells won with a separator that blocks slow parasitic currents while passing charge current. Insert a crested (triangular-profile SiO2/Si3N4/SiO2-type) tunnel barrier in the storage contact: at write/read bias the crest collapses and current flows, while at the few hundred mV seen in retention tunneling falls exponentially, starving the off-transistor leakage path.
why: Adds a >10^4 current nonlinearity between ~1 V and ~0.3 V in series with the subthreshold path (fact 3); could raise retention ~100x while keeping 10-20 ns access if the barrier stays thin.

title: Self-clearing film-capacitor electrode isolates leaky capacitor defects automatically
idea: Metallized-film power capacitors survive dielectric flaws because a local breakdown vaporizes the ultrathin electrode around the flaw, isolating it. Make the DRAM top plate locally ultrathin (2-3 nm TiN or Ru) over the high-k so a forming pulse at test burns open a nanometric hole around any leakage hot spot, removing that path while losing <1% of the cell's capacitor area.
why: Dielectric leakage defects set part of the retention tail and block thinner/higher-k films (facts 1, 3); self-clearing converts defect-tail cells into normal ones and lets the film be thinned for more fF.

title: AMOLED dual-gate TFT trick: breathing back-gate for hold versus access
idea: Display backplanes add a second gate under the TFT to shift its threshold on demand. Give vertical-channel 4F2 access transistors a shared back-gate plate held at about -1 V during retention (raising Vt ~0.3 V, cutting subthreshold leakage ~1000x) and pulsed positive only for the activated mat during access to boost on-current.
why: Decouples off-state leakage from on-current (facts 3, 10): longer refresh intervals and a lower VPP wordline swing because the back-gate supplies the on-boost.

title: Photoconductive switch from pulsed-power labs as an optically gated access device
idea: Pulsed-power and THz labs use photoconductive switches: wide-bandgap semiconductors that insulate in the dark and conduct when illuminated. Make the access element a GaN or ZnO photoconductive bridge under an on-chip SiN waveguide 'optical wordline'; dark off-current is set by a ~3.4 eV bandgap (sub-aA) and a ~1 ns light pulse opens it for read/write.
why: Removes the ~3 V wordline swing (fact 10) and the bandgap-limited leakage tail (fact 3); optical wordlines have no RC, allowing longer rows with fewer drivers (fact 7).

title: Solar MPPT perturb-and-observe loop tunes each bank's negative wordline
idea: Solar inverters find the maximum-power point by nudging voltage and watching the response. Off-state leakage versus negative wordline voltage has a minimum (subthreshold falls while GIDL rises), so an on-die loop nudges each bank's VNWL by +/-25 mV, reads a replica-transistor leakage integrator, and settles at that bank's minimum for its current temperature and age.
why: Fixed VNWL is set for worst-case corners; tracking the true minimum could cut tail leakage 2-3x across temperature and aging (fact 3) for negligible area.

title: Pinch-valve access: piezo-squeezed channel that physically closes the conduction path
idea: Pinch valves seal by squeezing a tube flat instead of holding back pressure. Build the access element from a piezoresistive Mott material (SmSe-type) clamped by a thin relaxor piezoelectric driven by the wordline: strained, the material goes metallic; unstrained, it is a wide-gap insulator, so there is no gate-controlled subthreshold tail at all.
why: Replaces exponential subthreshold behavior with a pressure-driven insulator-metal transition switching at ~0.1-0.3 V, attacking both the voltage floor (fact 10) and leakage (fact 3).

title: Time-release capsule: buried hydrogen reservoir re-passivates traps over product life
idea: Extended-release drugs meter an active ingredient for years from an embedded reservoir. Embed a hydrogen-rich silicon nitride layer, sealed above by a dense diffusion barrier, a few hundred nm below the cell array so it slowly releases hydrogen at 85 C operation and keeps re-passivating dangling bonds created by hot-carrier and VRT activity.
why: The retention tail drifts with aging and in-field VRT (fact 3); a self-replenishing passivant keeps the tail tight for 10 years and removes the ~2x end-of-life refresh guardband.

title: Cold-chain time-temperature indicator cells trigger refresh by accumulated thermal dose
idea: Vaccine shipments carry time-temperature indicators that integrate Arrhenius dose rather than trusting a schedule. In each subarray keep a few canary cells deliberately built leakier than the 6-sigma tail (wider junction implant); rewrite them at each refresh, poll them cheaply, and refresh the subarray only when a canary flips.
why: Spec refresh assumes 85 C worst case, but devices often run 45-65 C, so tracking real thermal dose cuts refresh 4-10x and most of the 16-33% idle refresh power (fact 3).

title: Astrophotography dark-frame subtraction: sense reference that tracks predicted decay
idea: Astronomers subtract a dark frame because dark current is predictable. Store a 2-bit leakage class per row from test, and lower the sense amplifier's reference (dummy-cell level) with time-since-refresh according to that class, so a partly decayed '1' still resolves against a reference that has 'decayed' alongside it.
why: Reclaims roughly half the sensing margin now spent on decay, giving 2-3x longer refresh intervals (fact 3) with no cell change.

title: Subsea pressure-compensated housings: park standby bitlines at the leaky state's level
idea: Deep-sea electronics survive by equalizing pressure instead of resisting it. During self-refresh, park bitlines at the stored-'1' voltage instead of VDD/2 so '1' cells (which also suffer junction leakage) see zero drain-source voltage and no subthreshold loss, while robust '0' cells' small upward subthreshold leak is partly offset by their own downward junction leak.
why: Targets the weakest state in the tail; could extend worst-case retention 2-4x in idle, where refresh is 16-33% of power (fact 3).

title: Water-utility pressure management: store a lower '1' level during standby
idea: Water utilities cut leaks by lowering night pressure because crack flow rises faster than linearly with pressure. On self-refresh entry, rewrite rows with a '1' of ~0.75 VARY instead of full VARY; GIDL and trap-assisted junction leakage fall super-linearly with storage-node voltage, so tail cells lose charge more slowly than the signal shrinks, and full levels are restored on exit.
why: Net retention gain of ~1.5-3x for GIDL-dominated tail cells plus lower CV^2 per standby refresh (facts 3, 10).

title: Regenerative braking for bitlines: recycle refresh charge into the next subarray
idea: Electric vehicles recover braking energy instead of burning it in friction brakes. After a subarray's refresh, before equalization, connect its high-side bitlines through a charge-sharing switch matrix to the next subarray's bitlines so the next refresh starts part-charged, recovering a further ~25-40% of bitline CV^2 beyond normal equalization.
why: Bitline swing dominates the ~46 fJ/bit refresh energy (fact 3); recycling could cut refresh energy 25-40% with no cell change.

title: Foveated rendering for memory: refresh low-order mantissa bit-planes far less
idea: VR headsets render full detail only where the eye looks. Store AI weights and KV caches bit-plane-wise so sign, exponent and top mantissa bits live in normally refreshed rows, while the lowest 3-5 mantissa bits of BF16/FP8 sit in rows refreshed 8-16x less often and are allowed rare flips.
why: For LLM-dominated DRAM, 30-50% of stored bits tolerate occasional errors; cuts refresh energy and bandwidth loss ~30-45% at 32-64 Gb (fact 3).

title: Airline departure board: compiler-published buffer lifetimes elide refresh entirely
idea: Airlines know every departure in advance and staff gates accordingly. AI accelerator compilers know statically when each activation or gradient buffer is next rewritten; they publish per-region lifetimes to the memory controller, which skips refresh for any row guaranteed to be rewritten or freed within tREFW.
why: Training activations live milliseconds, so 40-70% of HBM rows may never need refresh in such workloads, recovering much of the 10-20% bandwidth lost to refresh (fact 3).

title: Let out-of-the-money options expire: recomputable data receives no refresh
idea: Traders let options expire when exercising costs more than they are worth. Tag regions holding recomputable data (KV-cache blocks rebuildable from tokens, cached embeddings, prefetch buffers) as 'expire-allowed': they get long or no refresh, ECC flags any decayed line, and the runtime recomputes it on demand.
why: KV caches are a growing share of inference DRAM; dropping their refresh and accepting rare recompute saves refresh power and lets weaker-retention, cheaper dies serve them (fact 3, cost per bit).

title: Window-frame thermal break: keep HBM 25C cooler than its GPU
idea: Aluminum window frames got a polymer thermal break so cold never bridges to the warm side. Cut a low-conductivity trench (porous oxide or sealed void) through the interposer between the GPU and HBM footprints and give HBM its own colder coolant branch, holding DRAM near 60 C instead of 85-95 C.
why: Leakage roughly doubles per ~10 C and refresh doubles above 85 C; 25 C cooler cuts refresh ~4-6x and frees bandwidth (facts 3, 5).

title: Ugly-produce program: sell retention-failing dies with in-system refresh grades
idea: Grocers turned misshapen fruit from waste into a discounted product line. Bin DRAM dies by measured retention (32/64/128/256 ms grades at 85 C) instead of scrapping those that miss 64 ms, and sell low-retention grades to hyperscalers whose controllers apply per-module refresh rates read from SPD.
why: Retention fallout is real yield loss at advanced nodes; recovering even 3-8% of dies adds bit supply without new fabs (capital intensity, supply).

title: California 'One Watt' standby rule, applied to DRAM self-refresh power
idea: Standby-power regulation (the One Watt Initiative, California Title 20) pushed the appliance industry to redesign idle circuits within a few years. Propose an Energy-Star-style data-center label capping self-refresh/idle power per GB (e.g. <=0.5 mW/GB at 45 C), making low-leakage access devices and adaptive refresh a procurement criterion.
why: Refresh is 16-33% of idle power at 32-64 Gb (fact 3); a standard turns that into a purchasing metric and funds the access-device R&D the market underprices.

title: Pressure-cooker deuterium anneal replaces fluorine interface passivation of access gates
idea: Pressure cookers cook through at lower temperature by raising pressure. Instead of fluorine implants or F-containing gate stacks, run a 20-25 atm pure-D2 anneal at ~350 C after capacitor and BEOL so deuterium penetrates deep buried-wordline and vertical-channel interfaces that forming gas cannot reach; Si-D bonds resist hot-carrier and thermal depassivation better than Si-H.
why: Lower, more stable interface-trap density narrows the GIDL/trap-assisted tail (fact 3) by ~1.5-3x with zero fluorinated chemistry.

title: Vacuum-flask isolation: hydrogen-anneal voids float storage junctions above nothing
idea: A thermos keeps heat in by surrounding it with nothing. Etch a dense array of tiny holes with Cl2/HBr plasma beneath each storage-node region and anneal in H2 at ~1100 C so silicon surface migration seals them into a continuous buried void ('empty space in silicon'); the storage junction sits on vacuum, with no HF release etch or fluorinated gas.
why: Eliminates most of the junction's bottom-area depletion volume and its generation leakage toward the substrate (fact 3): ~2-5x lower junction leakage.

title: MEMS bulk-micromachining: TMAH crystallographic etch makes atomically smooth access pillars
idea: MEMS fabs carve mirror-flat silicon walls along slow-etching crystal planes with alkaline TMAH, no plasma. Define vertical access pillars with an amorphous-carbon hard mask opened in O2 plasma, rough-etch with Cl2/HBr, then finish sidewalls in dilute TMAH so channel faces terminate on crystal planes, replacing SF6/fluorocarbon etch and its damage and polymer residue.
why: Plasma-damaged, rough sidewalls set Dit in 4F2 vertical transistors; crystallographic faces could cut Dit 3-10x and tighten Vt spread, shrinking the leakage tail (fact 3) while dropping PFAS-class etch gases.

title: Sous-vide sealing: channel epi and gate oxide grown without air break
idea: Sous-vide food is sealed before cooking so nothing can contaminate it. Replace the HF-last pre-gate clean with a cluster tool that grows a fresh selective epitaxial silicon skin on the access-channel surface (SiH4/HCl/H2) and oxidizes it in situ by radical oxidation without breaking vacuum, so the gate interface is born clean and never touches hydrofluoric acid.
why: Pristine interfaces cut trap-assisted leakage and Vt variation (fact 3) and remove HF baths and their waste stream, easing U.S. fab permitting (U.S. manufacturability).

title: Lead-free solder playbook: molybdenum oxychloride wordlines end WF6 fluorine damage
idea: Electronics went lead-free in a coordinated material swap that ended up improving reliability. Replace WF6-deposited tungsten buried wordlines with molybdenum from MoO2Cl2 on a TiCl4-based TiN liner, plus a low-workfunction n+ poly cap on the storage-junction side (dual-workfunction gate), so no fluorine diffuses into the gate oxide and storage-side GIDL drops.
why: Removes fluorine-induced oxide traps and cuts GIDL (fact 3) while dropping reliance on Chinese tungsten (~80%); Mo also has lower resistivity at narrow widths for faster wordlines.

title: Vinyl-record pressing: nanoimprint wordline gratings with diamond-like-carbon release, not fluorosilanes
idea: Records are stamped from a master in seconds instead of each being cut. Pattern dense wordline and active-line gratings by UV nanoimprint from a master mold coated with hydrogenated diamond-like carbon as the anti-stick layer, using a PFAS-free acrylate resist, O2 plasma descum and Cl2/HBr transfer etch in place of fluorosilane release layers and PFAS photoacid generators.
why: Cuts EUV/immersion passes and capital (fact 4); master-replicated lines avoid stochastic EUV line-edge roughness, narrowing the access-transistor Vt and leakage tail (fact 3).

title: Batik wax-resist: hydrocarbon-inhibited selective deposition self-aligns GIDL offset spacers
idea: Batik artists block dye with wax so color lands only where intended. Use long-chain alkylsilane or alkanethiol inhibitors (no fluorinated SAMs) to block ALD on the gate metal while a SiN/SiOC offset grows only on the junction side, self-aligning a 2-3 nm gate-to-storage-junction underlap that weakens the field driving band-to-band GIDL.
why: Self-aligned underlap without extra lithography cuts GIDL, often the dominant tail mechanism, 3-10x (fact 3) and removes an overlay-limited step (fact 4).

title: Electrolytic-capacitor anodizing: alumina pore templates grow vertical access channels
idea: Aluminum electrolytic-capacitor makers anodize foil in oxalic or phosphoric acid, self-organizing billions of straight nanopores. Anodize a deposited aluminum film over the array (pitch 25-40 nm set by anodizing voltage), thin the pore-bottom barrier in phosphoric acid, then fill pores bottom-up with selective epitaxial silicon to form gate-all-around vertical access channels, with no fluorocarbon high-aspect-ratio etch anywhere.
why: Mask-free, self-assembled 4F2-class access pillars (facts 2, 4) with all-around gates for low leakage; replaces an EUV-patterned pillar etch with a wet bath.

title: Tea-bag steeping: molecular monolayer doping forms damage-free storage junctions
idea: A tea bag delivers flavor by surface contact, not force. Instead of implanting arsenic/phosphorus (or BF2 for p+), self-assemble a monolayer of phosphorus-bearing molecules such as diethyl vinylphosphonate on the storage-node contact, cap it with oxide and drive it in with a spike anneal, giving ultra-shallow junctions with no implant damage and no fluorine.
why: End-of-range implant defects are prime retention-tail trap sites (fact 3); damage-free junctions could tighten the tail 2-5x.

title: RV absorption fridge: GPU waste heat chills memory without fluorinated refrigerants
idea: Absorption refrigerators in RVs and hotels run on heat, using water/lithium-bromide or ammonia/water instead of HFC/HFO refrigerants. Drive a rack-level LiBr/water absorption chiller with the 60-90 C accelerator coolant return to make chilled water dedicated to HBM and DIMM cold plates at ~30 C.
why: Memory 30-40 C cooler cuts leakage ~8x and allows long refresh intervals (fact 3) using heat that is otherwise rejected, with no fluorinated refrigerant or PFAS immersion fluid.

title: Power-transformer ester oil: single-phase immersion keeps DIMMs cold, PFAS-free
idea: Grid transformers moved to biodegradable natural-ester oils for safe, fire-resistant cooling. Immerse memory modules, heat spreaders removed, in a forced-flow single-phase synthetic-hydrocarbon or natural-ester bath, replacing the fluorocarbon two-phase fluids now being phased out, and hold every DRAM die at a uniform ~40 C.
why: Uniform low temperature removes hot-spot-driven worst-case refresh and the 2x refresh mode above 85 C (fact 3), with no PFAS fluid.

title: Hand-warmer phase-change wax keeps HBM below the 85C refresh cliff
idea: Paraffin hand-warmers and chocolate tempering exploit a melting plateau to pin temperature. Pack a paraffin/graphite composite PCM melting at ~78 C into the HBM stack lid and mold cavity so burst workloads melt wax instead of pushing DRAM above 85 C, where JEDEC doubles the refresh rate.
why: Avoids the 2x refresh rate and its bandwidth loss during bursts (fact 3); paraffin is cheap and fluorine-free.

title: Pyrolytic self-cleaning oven: wordline heaters anneal VRT traps in the field
idea: Self-cleaning ovens periodically run very hot to burn off residue. In a maintenance window, migrate a bank's data, then drive current through its buried metal wordlines as resistive heaters to hold the array near 250 C for seconds, re-annealing VRT and hydrogen-related traps (as shown for NAND self-healing) before the data returns; no chemistry at all.
why: Resets the aging-driven retention tail (fact 3) so the end-of-life refresh guardband (~2x) can be dropped and VRT outliers are erased rather than mapped out.

title: Piano tuning: per-cell charge-trap trimming of leaky access transistor thresholds
idea: A piano tuner adjusts each string individually instead of rebuilding the piano. Add a thin LPCVD silicon-nitride charge-trap layer (dichlorosilane + ammonia, no fluorine) to the access gate stack; at wafer sort, find tail cells and apply hot-carrier program pulses through their own wordline and bitline to inject electrons and raise just their Vt by 150-300 mV.
why: A fluorine-free passivation flow leaves a slightly wider Vt tail; trimming the few-ppm worst cells collapses the leakage tail 10-100x (fact 3) so refresh is set by the median cell, not the outlier.

title: Rubber vulcanization: sulfur-healed MoS2 vertical access channels at back-end temperature
idea: Vulcanization uses sulfur to cure rubber's weak links. Grow bilayer MoS2 by MOCVD from Mo(CO)6 and H2S at <=450 C on the capacitor top as a vertical access channel, 'vulcanize' its sulfur vacancies (the dominant trap and leakage path) with an in-situ H2S anneal, and encapsulate with ALD alumina from TMA/water instead of fluoropolymer passivation.
why: A ~1.6 eV gap and sub-1 nm junctionless body give orders lower off-current than silicon (fact 3) and allow monolithic stacking of access layers (fact 2), fluorine-free end to end.

title: SF6 breakers to vacuum interrupters: nano vacuum-gap access switch
idea: The grid is replacing SF6 gas-insulated breakers with vacuum interrupters because vacuum insulates without fluorinated gas. Build a lateral 20-30 nm vacuum-gap field-emission switch, sealed by a PVD cap, whose emitter tip conducts only when the wordline gate thins the barrier; off-state current is Fowler-Nordheim limited and there is no substrate junction.
why: Removes junction and subthreshold leakage paths entirely (fact 3) with temperature-insensitive retention, and the cavity seal needs no fluorinated chemistry.

title: Cubic-zirconia skull melting: crucible-free silicon with fewer oxygen-related leakage traps
idea: Synthetic-gem makers melt zirconia inside a crust of its own frozen material in a water-cooled copper 'cold crucible'. Grow DRAM-grade silicon by cold-crucible induction Czochralski, eliminating the Spruce Pine high-purity quartz crucible and its oxygen supply, and engineer gettering with nitrogen/carbon co-doping instead of oxygen precipitates.
why: Lower interstitial oxygen means fewer oxygen-related defects and thermal donors near junctions (narrower tail, fact 3) and removes a >80% single-source chokepoint; crystal growth stays fluorine-free.

title: LCD panel laser repair: hydrogen-ambient spot anneal heals mapped tail cells
idea: Display fabs laser-repair defective pixels after test instead of scrapping panels. After retention mapping at wafer sort, scan a focused infrared laser through the thinned wafer backside in D2/H2 ambient over regions holding tail cells, briefly heating buried interfaces to re-passivate traps; only photons and hydrogen, no fluorine.
why: Repairs the few-ppm tail locally without adding thermal budget to the whole wafer, turning refresh-limiting cells normal (fact 3) and recovering retention-limited yield.

title: Microwave oven annealing: low-temperature regrowth of storage junction damage
idea: Microwave ovens heat what absorbs, not the whole kitchen. Activate storage-node dopants and regrow amorphized silicon by 2.45/5.8 GHz microwave annealing at 400-500 C, where dipole-assisted solid-phase epitaxy avoids the end-of-range loops and diffusion of spike anneals, replacing the fluorine co-implants used to suppress those defects.
why: Fewer end-of-range dislocation loops near the junction shrinks the generation-leakage tail (fact 3); the low temperature also suits monolithically stacked tiers (fact 2).

title: Thin-film solar liquid-phase crystallization: monocrystal-grade silicon for stacked access tiers
idea: Thin-film solar groups melt silicon on glass with a scanning line-focus diode laser so it recrystallizes into centimeter-scale grains. Apply line-laser liquid-phase crystallization to each deposited amorphous-silicon tier of a 3D DRAM, seeded through windows opened in an alumina inter-tier dielectric with hot phosphoric acid, to get near-single-crystal lateral access channels without fluorinated etch or wafer bonding.
why: Grain-boundary traps make stacked poly-Si access transistors too leaky; LPC silicon could approach bulk leakage, the key blocker for 26+ tier 3D DRAM (facts 2, 3).

title: Fractional-reserve banking: row-parity reserve absorbs fluorine-free process's wider tail
idea: Banks keep only a fraction of deposits on hand because withdrawals rarely coincide. Accept the wider retention tail of a hydrogen-passivated, fluorine-free process by adding one XOR parity row per 32-row group inside each subarray; refresh at an interval where at most one row per group is likely to hold a decayed cell, and rebuild that row from parity when ECC flags it.
why: Sets refresh near the 99.99th-percentile cell instead of the 6-sigma tail: 2-4x fewer refreshes (fact 3) for ~3% area, turning the constraint's yield penalty into design margin.

title: Coaxial cable shielding: grounded TiN sleeve kills passing-wordline leakage
idea: Coax stops signals coupling by wrapping them in a grounded shield. Wrap each buried wordline's passing segment, where it runs beside a neighbor's storage junction, with a thin grounded TiN sleeve deposited from TiCl4/NH3 (fluorine-free), so the passing gate cannot invert or field-stress the neighbor's junction edge.
why: Passing-gate-induced leakage and GIDL in neighbors is a known retention and disturb mechanism at 6F2/4F2 (facts 3, 9); shielding could cut that tail component >5x.

title: Shop-door air curtain: electrostatically doped storage junction with no dopant atoms
idea: An air curtain separates indoors from outdoors with no physical door. Form the storage-node 'n+ region' electrostatically: a low-workfunction metal contact (hafnium- or yttrium-based) on an undoped silicon tip induces an electron layer by workfunction difference, so there is no implanted junction, no dopant clusters and no BF2 or fluorine co-implant.
why: Without implanted dopants and their damage, generation sites and random-dopant Vt variation shrink, narrowing the leakage tail (fact 3) and removing implant steps (fact 4).
